sources_summary: FAA CY2024 ACAIS 'Enplanements at All Commercial Service Airports (by Rank)', published 9/15/2025; BTS/DOT Air Travel Consumer Report (Dec 2024, Full Year 2024 issue) Table 5 (Oct 2024 monthly, all airports) and BTS 'Table 4/6 Ranking of Major Airport On-Time Arrival/Departure Performance, Year-to-date thru Dec 2024' (Core 30 airports, full-year 2024); Wikipedia 'Airlines and destinations' tables retrieved 2026-08-11. See SOURCES.md for full citations.

BOS.ontime_period: 2024 annual (Jan 1 - Dec 31, 2024), BTS Table 6 'Ranking of Major Airport On-Time Departure Performance' (Core 30 airports only)
BOS.destinations_source_note: Wikipedia 'Airlines and destinations' table (Logan International Airport), retrieved 2026-08-11. Wikipedia tables reflect current schedules and may be stale/incomplete.
BOS.notes: FAA classifies BOS Large Hub. BTS annual on-time figures available because BOS is one of the DOT 'Core 30' largest airports.

MIA.destinations_source_note: Wikipedia 'Airlines and destinations' table (Miami International Airport), retrieved 2026-08-11 via Wikipedia section wikitext. NOTE: source content was very large (~100KB wikitext) and the extraction tool truncated before the final few airlines alphabetically (roughly JetBlue/LATAM/Southwest/Spirit/United/Turkish/Qatar); the list above is very likely missing a handful of long-haul destinations (e.g. Doha, Istanbul) that those carriers may serve. Flagged as an incompleteness limitation.
MIA.notes: Large Hub. Destination list is the largest and most Caribbean/Latin-America-weighted of the 28 airports, consistent with MIA's role as the primary US-Latin America gateway; treat the list as near-complete but not exhaustive per the truncation note above.
